PullRequest.Title: agentHost: Attribute and reduce agent Host turn pre-send latency
PullRequest.Body:
Part of the VS-Code-side work for the Agent Host TTFT investigation (microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8816).

## Problem

Agent Host reports `timeToFirstProgress` as a single opaque number emitted at turn completion. It covers the whole host pre-send path, but attributes nothing — so when Agent Host TTFT looks worse than Local, there is no way to tell which piece of host work is responsible without re-investigating from scratch each time.

While adding that attribution I found and fixed the two largest contributors it exposes.

## 1. Stage attribution

`agentHost.turnCompleted` gains six measurements:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `sendStageWorkingDirectoryMs` | Working-directory resolution, incl. first-send worktree creation |
| `sendStageModelSelectionMs` | Applying model + agent selection on the provider |
| `sendStageAttachmentsMs` | Resolving chat attachments |
| `sendStageContributionsMs` | Outgoing-turn chat contributions |
| `sendStageCheckpointMs` | Residual wait on the turn-start checkpoint |
| `timeToProviderDispatch` | **Total host cost before the provider is called** |

Design notes:

- These use a **new `AgentHostTurnSendStage` vocabulary rather than widening `AgentHostTurnFailureStage`**. "Where did the turn break" and "where did the turn spend its time" are different questions, and `failureStage` / `currentStage` have live dashboards that shouldn't shift meaning. Both existing fields are untouched.
- Durations are measured off the turn's **existing stopwatch**, so they share a clock with `timeToFirstProgress` and can be subtracted from it.
- **`0` and absent are distinct**: a stage that ran instantly reports `0`; a stage that never ran (ephemeral session → no checkpoint, subagent turn → no send path) is omitted.
- A turn that ends mid-stage still attributes its partial cost — `turnCompleted` closes any open stage rather than dropping it.

## 2. Turn-start checkpoint now overlaps instead of blocking

`captureTurnStartCheckpoint` ran a full git working-tree snapshot **inline before `sendMessage`**: `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all`, temp index, `read-tree HEAD`, stage changed paths, `write-tree`. Measured on this repo:

```
cold:  status 382ms + read-tree 509ms + write-tree 110ms = ~1,001 ms
warm:  ~424-457 ms  (3 consecutive runs)
```

That ran on **every turn** of every non-ephemeral session with a working directory, before the prompt reached the SDK. Local Copilot Chat has no equivalent pre-send git snapshot.

It now starts as soon as the working directory is known, so it overlaps the model-selection round trips, attachment resolution and contributions — and is **still awaited before `sendMessage`**. The invariant is unchanged: the snapshot always completes before the agent sees the prompt, so this is safe for all three providers with no provider-side changes.

Two correctness points the tests pin down:

- A turn **already cancelled** before the send path reaches this point never captures at all — the snapshot is expensive and would only be discarded. (`cancellation before send skips turn-start capture` covers this.)
- Cancellation now needs a **second discard**. The cancel-time discard fires before the concurrent capture settles, so it removes nothing; without the follow-up discard a cancelled turn would retain a checkpoint. The new test asserts the exact `capture:start → discard → capture:end → discard` ordering.

## 3. Model selection no longer waits on an in-flight catalog refresh

`_validateModelSelection` awaited any in-flight model-catalog refresh — a network round-trip — on every turn that carried a model. That await exists only to avoid falsely rejecting a model a pending refresh is about to add. A model **already in the catalog** cannot be invalidated by a refresh landing later, so that case now returns immediately. Unknown models still wait, and the empty-catalog fail-open behaviour is unchanged.

## Deliberately not included

`sendStageModelSelectionMs` / `sendStageContributionsMs` will now show whether collapsing the `changeModel`/`changeAgent` round trips or moving the title-metadata SQLite read off the send path is worth doing, and `sendStageCheckpointMs` will show how much the checkpoint still costs after overlapping (i.e. whether deferring it behind a `PreToolUse` edit barrier justifies the cross-provider hook work). Those are left until the data says so rather than optimised blind.

This PR also does **not** address the measurement-artifact half of the issue — the eval dashboard still compares different boundaries and different agent steps between Local and Agent Host. That needs the user-perceived first-progress metric, which is separate follow-up work.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed ordering, full Git subprocess chain, catch ordering, and session serialization are directly visible in code and covered by the new cancellation test. Exact duration varies by repository size and cache warmth, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Git subprocesses, temporary-index filesystem I/O, and per-session checkpoint queue time
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The wasted work runs once per failed/cancelled pre-dispatch turn for every working directory; within each directory it scans the repository and stages every changed path, and all captures/discards are serialized by session.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Delayed error reporting and delayed dispatch of a subsequent turn, with unnecessary CPU, disk I/O, and subprocess activity after the original turn can no longer reach the provider.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The turn-start checkpoint was created only after model selection, attachment resolution, contributions, and the first cancellation check. A rejection or cancellation during those stages therefore dispatched the error or returned without running checkpoint Git commands.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The diff starts capture immediately after working-directory resolution. On any later pre-provider failure, the added catch path awaits `_discardPendingTurnStartCheckpoint`, which first awaits the full capture; cancellation cleanup is likewise sequenced behind the capture.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 1753 starts the expensive checkpoint before model selection, attachments, and contributions, and added line 1805 awaits its cleanup on pre-provider failure. In the base code the capture call was below all of those stages and the cancellation check, so these abort paths never incurred or waited for it.
Findings.Title: Do not block pre-send failures on the speculative checkpoint
Findings.Impact: If model validation rejects, attachment or contribution resolution fails, or the user cancels during those stages, the host still runs git status, read-tree, optional git add, and write-tree for each workspace. The error is not dispatched until this completes, and a quick retry's checkpoint queues behind the abandoned capture.
Findings.Evidence: `captureTurnStartCheckpoint` calls `captureWorkingTreeAsTree` per working directory. That implementation launches repository-wide `git status --untracked-files=all`, `git read-tree`, optional `git add` over all changed paths, and `git write-tree`, with temp-directory I/O. `AgentHostCheckpointService` uses one `SequencerByKey` per session, and the new cancellation test explicitly establishes that capture finishes before discard. Added line 1805 awaits the helper before constructing and dispatching `ChatError`; the helper awaits the capture before queueing discard.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the overlap for successful sends, but make turn-start capture cancellable: check turn liveness before each queued repository snapshot and propagate an abort signal to active Git commands. On pre-provider failure, surface the error immediately and await only bounded cleanup rather than completion of the abandoned snapshot.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Every non-ephemeral turn synchronously awaited its turn-start checkpoint immediately before provider dispatch. The checkpoint traverses each working directory and runs git status, read-tree, optional git add, and write-tree plus temporary filesystem work, so that entire repository-scaled subprocess chain sat on time-to-first-provider progress.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Agent Host turns incur avoidable pre-provider latency from a full Git working-tree snapshot, scaling with working directories and changed paths.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The capture now starts as soon as working-directory resolution completes and runs concurrently with model selection, attachment resolution, and outgoing contributions; only its residual duration is awaited before provider dispatch.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 1762 awaited captureTurnStartCheckpoint directly after all other pre-send stages and immediately before setting the provider stage. AgentHostCheckpointService._captureTurnStartCheckpoint calls getRepositoryRoot and captureWorkingTreeAsTree for every working directory; captureWorkingTreeAsTree runs git status, read-tree, optional git add, write-tree, and temporary-directory I/O. The added call at line 1753 starts that same promise earlier while the subsequent selection/attachment/contribution work proceeds, reducing the serialized critical path without changing the before-dispatch invariant.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Model selection awaited any in-flight catalog refresh before validating even when the requested model was already present in the published catalog. The refresh reaches client.rpc.models.list, so an unrelated catalog RPC/network round trip serialized every affected turn's model-selection stage before provider dispatch.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Turns selecting an already-known model can have their provider dispatch and first response delayed by an unrelated in-flight model-catalog request.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: For ordinary refreshes, validation now returns immediately when the model is already present; only unknown models or credential/client-invalidating refreshes retain the wait.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 5102 unconditionally awaited _scheduledModelRefresh or _modelRefreshInFlight. _refreshModels calls _listModels, whose line 3000 awaits client.rpc.models.list. The added fast path at line 5135 checks the current catalog and returns for a known model unless an invalidating refresh is active; the included test gates models.list and proves changeModel reaches the SDK while that request remains in flight.

Scenarios.Scenario: Successful non-ephemeral top-level turn with one or more working directories
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Working-directory resolution completes first. The turn-start checkpoint now begins concurrently with model/agent selection, attachment resolution, and outgoing contributions, but its residual work must still complete before `agent.chats.sendMessage` dispatches to the provider. This reduces the prior serialized checkpoint cost.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each repository and capture its working tree via Git status, read-tree, optional add, and write-tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per working directory per turn; at least status/read-tree/write-tree, plus git add when changed paths exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same per-directory Git snapshot ran on every successful non-ephemeral turn, but it began only after model selection, attachments, and contributions and therefore its full duration was serialized immediately before provider dispatch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The capture overlaps other pre-send stages but any residual duration blocks provider dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the session database, create the turn record, and read its checkpoint ref.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same database work ran later and entirely on the pre-provider critical path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs inside the overlapping checkpoint and its residual duration remains before provider dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply model and agent selection through the provider chat abstraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one changeModel and one changeAgent operation per turn, co-started and awaited together.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same selection operations completed before checkpoint capture began.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before attachments/contributions and provider dispatch, but now overlaps the Git checkpoint.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is one checkpoint per turn, with one sequential repository snapshot per resolved working directory and staging proportional to the number of changed paths in each repository.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Model and agent selection are joined with `Promise.all`; the checkpoint overlaps those selections and subsequent attachment/contribution stages. Within a checkpoint, working directories are processed sequentially, and all checkpoint operations for a session are serialized by `SequencerByKey`.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A turn-start snapshot is captured every successful non-ephemeral turn; there is no positive or negative cache for the working-tree snapshot. Git/OS warm caches can lower duration but do not change command cardinality. The captured trees are retained only until end-of-turn capture or explicit discard.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed scheduling, per-directory loops, Git subprocesses, and before-dispatch await are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository size, changed-path count, number of workspace roots, and cache warmth determine how much checkpoint time remains after overlap.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression on successful turns; this path removes serialized checkpoint latency while preserving the existing boundary count.

Scenarios.Scenario: Turn cancelled or rejected during model selection, attachment resolution, or outgoing contributions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The speculative checkpoint starts after working-directory resolution. A pre-provider failure enters the catch block, which awaits capture completion through `_discardPendingTurnStartCheckpoint` before dispatching `ChatError`. Cancellation marks the turn complete independently, but discard and any subsequent turn's checkpoint remain queued behind the abandoned capture.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run Git status, read-tree, optional add, and write-tree for a turn that never reaches the provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One command sequence per working directory for each cancellation/failure after checkpoint start.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Checkpoint capture occurred after all these failure-prone stages and after a cancellation check, so the same aborted turns performed zero checkpoint Git snapshots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly delays pre-send error reporting because the catch awaits capture cleanup, and indirectly delays the next turn through the session sequencer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create/write/delete a temporary Git index directory and pathspec file, plus database turn creation for the abandoned checkpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One temporary index per working directory and one database turn operation per abandoned capture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These operations did not run for turns failing or cancelled before the old checkpoint location.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of the capture that must settle before the failure path continues and before queued session checkpoint work can proceed.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One newly wasted snapshot per aborted turn, multiplied by working-directory count and each repository's total scan/changed-path set.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The snapshot runs concurrently with pre-send work, but checkpoint capture and discard are serialized per session. A subsequent turn's checkpoint cannot overtake the cancelled/failed capture.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no reusable result because the snapshot is discarded. Warm filesystem caches may reduce individual Git durations, but every aborted turn still launches a fresh command sequence; failures are not negatively cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the new test proves capture completes before discard, and production code shows both the Git chain and per-session serialization.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The frequency of pre-dispatch cancellation/failure and exact Git duration vary, but invalid model rejection and user cancellation are realistic and repositories can make each capture materially slow.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity eager-work regression because abandoned turns now consume repository-scaled subprocess/I/O work and failure handling waits for it.

Scenarios.Scenario: Model selection while the model catalog refreshes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For an ordinary refresh and a model already in the published catalog, validation now returns immediately and provider selection proceeds. Unknown models still await the in-flight refresh; credential/client-invalidating refreshes also remain on the critical path before any cached model is trusted.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke Copilot SDK `client.rpc.models.list` to enumerate the model catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced request per refresh, not per selecting turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every selection carrying a model awaited any scheduled or in-flight catalog request before checking the cached list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Removed from the critical path for known-model selections during ordinary refresh; retained for misses and invalidating credential/client transitions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Catalog lookup is linear in the small published model list. At most one coalesced model refresh promise is awaited; the change does not fan out requests per model or turn.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Ordinary refresh remains independently in flight while known-model selection proceeds. Invalidating refreshes are coalesced by the scheduled deferred and serialize affected selections until the replacement catalog lands.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The published model list acts as the positive cache. Known hits bypass ordinary refreshes; misses and invalidating states await the single in-flight refresh. Failed refreshes retain the last known-good catalog as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: `_validateModelSelection` directly gates on the cache and tests hold the RPC open while proving a known selection completes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Refresh latency and overlap frequency vary with provider/network conditions, but the critical-path removal is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Performance improvement, not a regression; recorded as a regression fix with base blame.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Turn completion closes at most one open stage, copies references to a five-entry duration map, and emits the existing single `agentHost.turnCompleted` event with six additional numeric measurements. This occurs after the turn is already terminal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize six additional numeric/undefined fields in the existing turn-completed telemetry event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing event per completed turn; no additional event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The event omitted these six scalar fields.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Post-terminal bounded telemetry work; it does not delay provider dispatch or rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant bounded work per completed turn: at most five stage keys and six scalar telemetry properties.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous in-memory bookkeeping on completion; no new queue, fan-out, or parallel boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Per-turn timing state is removed on completion, so the added map does not accumulate across completed turns.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: map size and event cardinality are fixed by the five-stage union and one completion call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Telemetry transport implementation cost is not inspected, but the added payload is strictly bounded and reuses an existing event.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; bounded constant allocation and serialization.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all eight changed files. Submitted one finding for repository-scaled checkpoint work newly performed and awaited on cancelled/failed pre-send turns. Recorded two genuine regression fixes: overlapping turn-start Git snapshots with other pre-send work, and bypassing ordinary in-flight model refreshes for cached model hits. Telemetry attribution is bounded and lifecycle-clean.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
